title: Migration plan and timelines for legacy streaming and embeddings endpoints
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: This PRD defines the deprecation and migration requirements for two legacy surface areas: the real-time streaming endpoints ("chat.stream.v0" family) and the old embeddings endpoint ("embeddings/v1-legacy"). These legacy APIs were built prior to standardized output framing and unified token accounting, and they complicate routing, observability, and billing parity across Dedicated/Private/Hosted environments.
Goal: provide a clear migration path to the consolidated generate/chat and embeddings endpoints, provide tooling and SDK support to transition customers, and coordinate a predictable 9-month deprecation window with staged communications and rollouts.
Scope:
- Affected endpoints: chat.stream.v0.*, embeddings/v1-legacy
- Affected SDKs: node, python, go (all clients with streaming and legacy embeddings helpers)
- Affected runtimes: hosted API, Dedicated clusters (controlled shutdown only after customer confirmation), Private deployments (customer-managed; guidance + opt-in migration tooling)
Out of scope:
- Internal test-only endpoints, third-party partner private integrations where contractually restricted (handled case-by-case).
scope_changes:
Initial scope included an automatic server-side redirect for legacy streaming to the new streaming-compatible chat.generate endpoint. After review with engineering, we narrowed scope:
- Remove server-side automatic redirect for legacy streaming (too risky for real-time semantics differences).
- Provide a compatibility shim in SDKs that preserves framing for 90 days post-shutdown for customers who opt-in.
- Add a Dedicated migration concierge offering for customers with >100k concurrent tokens/day (separate SOW).
These changes were approved by Eng and Legal on 2026-03-05 and increase the estimated effort by ~20%.
acceptance_criteria: Public announcement published with migration guide and mapping table to new endpoints
Documentation: unified API spec updated with examples for streaming and batch embeddings
SDKs: node/python/go release with migration helpers and a deprecation warning emitted on first use
Compatibility: compatibility shim available for SDKs that can be toggled off by customers
Integration tests: end-to-end tests for migrated customers passing in staging and canary
Telemetry: dashboard that shows adoption metrics (requests hitting legacy vs new endpoints) live in Console
Billing: legacy endpoints are aligned to modern token accounting before shutdown or will be grandfathered with explicit billing note
Dedicated/private: runbook and checklist for Dedicated and Private customers signed off by partner engineering
migration_timeline: Phase 0 (2026-03-15 to 2026-04-15): Finalize mapping and publish technical migration guide + sample PRs and test corpus. Phase 1 (2026-04-16 to 2026-06-15): SDK releases (node v5.3.0, python v3.12.0, go v2.8.0) with migration helpers and deprecation warnings; start passive telemetry collection. Phase 2 (2026-06-16 to 2026-09-30): Active outreach to customers using legacy endpoints; dedicated concierge for high-usage customers; compatibility shim enabled by default in SDKs. Phase 3 (2026-10-01 to 2026-11-15): Final migration cutover window; disable legacy endpoint writes for hosted API but keep read-only logs for 30 days. Phase 4 (2026-11-16): Permanent shutdown of hosted legacy endpoints. Private/Dedicated: stop providing service-level support for legacy endpoints after 2026-11-16; customers can run compatibility shim independently but no Redwood SLA will be provided after that date.
sdk_migration_notes:
Node/Python/Go SDK teams will add: 1) helper: migrateStreaming(oldStreamRequest) -> new streaming request payload + example. 2) deprecation warning emitted via console.warn/logging on first legacy use and an instrumentation event to telemetry. 3) compatibility shim (opt-in flag: legacyCompatibility: true) that mints temporary framing to match older consumers. SDKs must be backward-compatible; patch-level install should opt-out of breaking changes. Deliverables:
- Node v5.3.0 (PR #1280)
- Python v3.12.0 (PR #442)
- Go v2.8.0 (PR #76)
Release branches must include test-suite that replays sample sessions from the legacy corpus.
rollout_plan: Canary: 2-week canary for SDKs and hosted routing changes targeting 5% of traffic in us-west-2. Observe errors, latency regressions, and customer behavioral analytics. If error rate >0.5% or median latency regresses >25ms over baseline for the canary cohort, pause and roll back changes. Gradual ramp: after canary success, ramp to 25% for 2 weeks, then 75% for 2 weeks, then global. Cutover: for hosted API, disable legacy write endpoints on 2026-11-16 at 00:00 UTC. For Dedicated, schedule per-customer cutover windows and require customer signoff two weeks before scheduled shutdown. For Private, provide a migration bundle and decommission guidance; Redwood will not forcibly shut Private deployments but will stop providing compatibility support after 2026-11-16.
communication_plan:
- 2026-03-15: Public blog post + email to all accounts announcing deprecation timeline and reasons.
 - 2026-04-01: In-product banner for customers currently using legacy endpoints (targeted based on telemetry).
 - 2026-05-01 to 2026-09-30: Account outreach: high-touch for top 200 legacy users, templated guidance for the rest.
 - 30/60/90-day reminder emails leading to shutdown.
 - Developer office hours weekly for 12 weeks starting 2026-04-01 (recordings published).
 - Post-shutdown: publish a deprecation report with lessons learned and adoption metrics.
risk_and_mitigations: Risk: Real-time semantics mismatch between legacy streaming and new streaming API can break low-latency apps. Mitigation: Provide compatibility shim, expand the canary cohort to include at least 10 customers with real-time use-cases, and add synthetic tests that mimic sub-200ms response expectations. Risk: Billing disputes due to different token accounting. Mitigation: Offer a two-month billing grace period for affected customers and provide detailed token usage reports. Risk: Private deployments may not upgrade; Mitigation: provide migration bundle + clear upgrade doc and offer paid migration assistance for large customers.
